facts.text: Drill Holes was deployed at Gale Crater during Curiosity (MSL) in 2013.

Curiosity has drilled dozens of holes into Martian bedrock, each about 1.6 cm wide and up to 6.5 cm deep. The powdered rock is delivered to the SAM and CheMin instruments inside the rover. Early drill samples at Yellowknife Bay revealed clay minerals and evidence of an ancient freshwater lake environment suitable for microbial life.
Engineered specifically to operate in the harsh vacuum and extreme temperatures of the Martian environment.
Delivered powdered rock to SAM and CheMin instruments, revealing clay minerals and organic molecules in Martian bedrock for the first time.
Dozens of drill holes across Gale Crater mark Curiosity's path, each one a tiny window into Mars's ancient chemistry.
